h1: Sri Panwa Phuket — pool villas on a clifftop cape that sell the view, not the beach
intro: Most people picture a beachfront resort when they imagine luxury in Phuket, but Sri Panwa took a different route — it climbed to the top of Cape Panwa on the island's southeastern tip and scattered private pool villas down the hillside, each with a 12-metre infinity pool facing the Andaman Sea. Open since 2004, it is still one of the first names that comes up for luxury in Phuket, especially thanks to BABA Nest, a rooftop bar ranked among the best in the world. Pool villas start from approx. THB 15,000/night.

BABA Nest rooftop bar at the top of the cape with 360-degree views at sunset
Inside a private modern-Thai pool villa with its own infinity pool out front

body.html: Sri Panwa's appeal starts on the drive up the hill. The resort sits on Cape Panwa, a headland jutting into the sea, so many villas look out over water on almost every side — this is not a beachfront hotel where you walk onto the sand, but a clifftop resort that sells views and privacy. Spread across more than 40 acres, it has one- and two-bedroom pool villas, Pool Suites and large residences, each set far enough apart to feel like your own holiday home.

The heart of every room is the 12-metre infinity pool out front. You can walk from the bed straight into the water in the morning without seeing another soul — an image reviewers mention again and again. The design is modern-Thai in wood and white tones, with an outdoor sala and a semi-open rain shower. Many guests say that once they settle into the villa they barely want to leave, because everything they need is in one place.
"Slipped into the pool at sunrise and saw nothing but sea and islands — no buildings, no other guests. It felt like we'd rented the whole headland to ourselves."

BABA Nest is the star that put Sri Panwa on the map. It's a rooftop bar at the highest point of the cape, around 60 metres above the sea, with a shallow pool wrapping the seating so the view reflects in the water at sunset. Seats are limited and the sunset slot fills fast, so book ahead. Even non-guests drive up for a cocktail — if you're staying here, set aside one evening just for BABA Nest.

Beyond the bar there are several BABA restaurants — Thai, Japanese and Chinese — plus a pool club beside the large forest waterfall pool. Cool Spa earns praise for its views and treatments. Service overall is described as warm and attentive, especially the team that handles proposals and weddings, which is why so many couples choose this place. Breakfast, though, is the point reviews call merely average for the price band — the real food is at the a la carte restaurants.

The thing to know before booking is the location. Cape Panwa is at the far end of the island, roughly 45 minutes to an hour from Phuket airport and a fair distance from Patong and the old town. If you want to head out for dinner or sightseeing you'll be calling a car every time, and it takes a while. Within the resort the lanes are steep and villas sit at different levels, so you rely on the hotel buggies — guests with mobility needs should flag this in advance.

A score of 8.9 from 2,600+ reviews on Agoda and 4.5 stars on TripAdvisor paints a clear picture — people who come to switch off, celebrate a special occasion or honeymoon tend to give top marks, while those expecting city-hotel convenience, or comparing the price to other Phuket villas, sometimes feel certain parts (breakfast, transfers) don't quite match the rate. Put plainly, Sri Panwa is buying 'a view and privacy'. If those two things are what you want, it delivers very well.

Tips drawn from reviews: ask for a villa facing the eastern side if you like sunrises, and book your BABA Nest sunset slot the moment you check in. Families are better off in a two-bedroom pool villa or residence than booking two separate rooms. And on departure day, leave more time than usual for the long drive down the cape.

honestSummary: Sri Panwa is at its best for travellers who want to switch off in a private pool villa with sea views and let the hotel be the destination — the privacy, the 360° views and BABA Nest are hard to find elsewhere in Phuket. Just accept that it's remote, you'll always need a car, and a few details (breakfast) don't fully live up to the price.
honestChecks: If you plan to eat out, hit the beaches and shop every day — Cape Panwa is at the far end of the island and the round trips eat up time → consider a hotel in Patong/Bang Tao that's easier to get out of
If steep walks are hard for you — villas sit at different hillside levels and rely on buggies → ask the hotel in advance for a villa near the service points
If you want to step straight onto the sand from your room — this is a clifftop resort, not a beachfront one → a hotel directly on the beach will suit you better

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Sri Panwa Phuket

faq.q: Where is Sri Panwa in Phuket — is it far?
faq.a: Sri Panwa sits atop Cape Panwa on the far southeastern tip of Phuket island. It's roughly 45 minutes to an hour from Phuket airport and a fair distance from Patong and the old town. It's a clifftop resort rather than a beachfront one, built around views and privacy, so you'll need a car whenever you head out.

faq.q: What does Sri Panwa cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: From approx. THB 15,000/night for a Pool Suite. A one-bedroom pool villa with a private infinity pool starts around THB 22,000, with two-bedroom villas and large residences above that. Rates are very seasonal and climb fast in high season — compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What is BABA Nest and do I need to book ahead?
faq.a: BABA Nest is a rooftop bar at the highest point of the cape with 360-degree views, ranked among the world's most beautiful rooftop bars. Seats are limited and the sunset slot fills fast, so reserve at check-in. Even non-guests can come up, but a booking is needed.

faq.q: Who is Sri Panwa best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples, honeymoons and special-occasion trips who want to switch off in a private pool villa. It suits travellers who treat the hotel as the destination rather than planning to go out every day. Larger families can take a two-bedroom villa or a residence.

faq.q: What is breakfast like at Sri Panwa?
faq.a: Most reviews say breakfast is average for a hotel in this class. The stronger food is at the a la carte BABA restaurants — Thai, Japanese and Chinese. Check whether your package includes breakfast when you book.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: In high season (November–April) book 1–2 months ahead, as the best-view villas and long-weekend dates fill quickly. Most platforms offer a Free Cancellation option — pick that if your plans aren't firm, then confirm later.
